text:
noah: seeing nondet eval outputs on CI for quantized-mistral-v2 even though the seed is printed and identical across runs. two runs with same seed give different generations for the same prompts.

elaine: ugh, any diffs in docker image or fastmath flags?

noah: we pinned the image. kernel build hash is the same. here's the runner log snippet:
```
INFO seed=12345678 model=quant-mistral-v2-k8 build=2026-03-10-1142
Sampling params: temperature=0.7 top_p=0.92 top_k=50
Resuming from checkpoint, kv_cache_resume=true
```

sam: kv_cache_resume + quant kernels have historically had tiny fp rounding diffs that can change top_p thresholds. could be hitting a tie-breaker in sampling.

noah: that's my suspicion. but weird part: the CI metric (perplexity / rouge) sometimes flips sign of regression depending on aggregation (mean vs median). so even same batch of outputs yields downstream flaky alerts.

karen: are we logging full RNG state? maybe worker pool seeding differs when we resume.

noah: currently we log only the seed printed above. not the RNG stream offsets.

elaine: quick experiment: stop worker reuse, run single-threaded with explicit PRNG state dumps and deterministic sampler. also force deterministic top_p comparator (tie-break by lower token id).

sam: +1. also try setting top_p to a fixed float with higher precision, e.g. 0.920000001, to see if rounding boundary is the issue.

noah: kicked off a manual run on a dedicated box with --single-thread --dump-prng before/after sampling. ci-bot started a compare job: https://ci.internal/runs/2159876543/compare

ci-bot: manual-run 2159876543 finished: outputs diverged at token 12, branching token probabilities: [0.2112, 0.2089] vs [0.2112, 0.2090] -> chose different token due to tie resolution.

noah: those tiny prob diffs align with quant kernel fp issues. interestingly, when I re-ran with quantization config QAT-v2 (slightly different rounding) the outputs matched across runs.

karen: ok so root cause chain: quantized kernel rounding + resume kv cache ordering + non-deterministic worker assignment -> tiny prob perturbation -> sampling tie resolves differently -> downstream metric flip when using mean.

elaine: proposals: 1) make sampling comparator deterministic (tie-break by token id), 2) log full PRNG stream offsets in CI, 3) change eval dashboard to use median or truncated-mean as default for alerts.

sam: also add a CI-only flag to force deterministic math mode for quant kernels (if possible) so evaluations are reproducible for regression checks.

noah: I'll implement deterministic comparator and PRNG dumps. can we change the dashboard threshold quickly? the current alert fired a Pager last night. :grimacing:

karen: we can change alerting config to median-based for now. I'll open a quick PR.

ci-bot: deploy of alert-config branch queued (deploy-1234).

noah: thanks. Will follow up with reproducibility run artifacts attached to the ticket.

elaine: massive :100: on adding deterministic tie-break — low-risk and should reduce a lot of false positives.

sam: leaving a note in the eval-runner README about resume/kv caveats for quant models.

noah: filing ticket with reproducer and artifacts: https://go/rdw/issue/9842

karen: assigned to noah, milestone: sprint-2026-03-3

noah: thanks all, will update thread when PRs land. :sparkles:
